current_trace: The build script parses autoresolve.combat_round_seconds as f64 and rejects values that are non-finite or not positive. It emits that same f64 using Debug formatting as an f32-suffixed source literal inside AnimationElapsed::from_seconds.

For a changed authored value such as 1e-100, with all other required inputs left admissible, source-level decimal and binary32 rounding imply a positive finite f64 and a zero f32 literal: this value is far below half the smallest binary32 subnormal. AnimationElapsed::from_seconds permits zero, so the generated expression does not itself reject that result. No input, code generation, compile or runtime scenario was executed. Whether the generated literal passes the selected compiler and lint configuration is not established; no successfully built or runnable counterexample is claimed.

AutoresolveParameters::validate rejects a zero combat_round_seconds, but the shown resolve_battle entry point takes EMBEDDED_AUTORESOLVE_PARAMETERS directly and does not call that validator before forwarding it. The selected joint-melee code derives its step count and window duration from that value. This establishes a conditional source path, not observed battle behavior.

Other emitted positive raw f32 fields and zero-accepting duration wrappers require the same f64-to-f32 admission review. PositiveSpeed differs: its constructor rejects zero, so an underflow there is not the same silent admitted state. The imported fatigue and contact objects are already f32 and their displayed validators execute in the build path; do not transfer the f64 argument to those fields.

The separate tactical default and external startup paths parse and validate TacticalCombatConfig, which invokes its autoresolve validator. Their validation does not by itself establish the strategic build-generated constant was revalidated.
